fact: Cameroon is one of the CEMAC states on GIMACPAY, the regional platform that processed 20.3 million transactions worth FCFA 863 billion in 2025, with the BEAC among its 153 participants.
BEAC's official entry into PAPSS was set for 9 July 2026, but banks and payment providers of the CEMAC zone must still connect technically before customers are served, per Africtelegraph.

Cameroon is one of six CEMAC states covered by GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard, validated by the UMAC ministerial committee in April 2026 and launched on 29 July 2026 over GIMACPAY, in service since 2021.
BEAC, the central bank of the CEMAC states, joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), per Afreximbank on 9 July 2026, with CEMAC banks to be connected by end-2026.

TechAfrica News reports on 9 July 2026 that BEAC, which serves Cameroon among six CEMAC states, has officially joined PAPSS, with PAPSS working with BEAC through end 2026 to operationalise the membership.
BEAC publishes Gimacpay's figures and notes delays in applying the interoperability framework set by governor's instruction n°001/GR/2018 for card payment systems in the Cemac zone.

AfricaNenda says the regional central bank BEAC, whose rules apply to the six CEMAC states including Cameroon, regulates payment market structures including technical approvals and authorisations of payment solutions.
AfricaNenda says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY, is its overseer and settlement agent, and the switch serves payment providers in Cameroon.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, provides interoperable payment services to providers in the six CEMAC states including Cameroon.
BEAC launched the interoperable CEMAC QR code on 29 July 2026 in Douala, with regional interbank operations routed and cleared via GIMAC.
BEAC says the interoperable QR code covers the six CEMAC countries, cleared through GIMAC, under Regulation 02/26/CEMAC/UMAC/COREFI of 8 April 2026.
